evidence.quote: scientific study and reflection had taught us that the known universe of three dimensions embraces the merest fraction of the whole cosmos of substance and energy
evidence.paraphrase: The narrators frame the phenomenon in terms of a multidimensional cosmos exceeding the familiar three dimensions.

evidence.quote: certain unfamiliar and unclassified modifications of vital force and attenuated matter; existing very infrequently in three-dimensional space because of its more intimate connection with other spatial units
evidence.paraphrase: They hypothesize an entity as a modification of vital force and matter tied to other spatial dimensions.

evidence.quote: still operative through rare and unknown laws of atomic and electronic motion
evidence.paraphrase: The lingering influence is attributed to unknown laws of atomic and electronic motion.

evidence.quote: Such a thing was surely not a physical or biochemical impossibility in the light of a newer science which includes the theories of relativity and intra-atomic action.
evidence.paraphrase: The possibility of the entity is justified by reference to relativity and intra-atomic science.

evidence.quote: One might easily imagine an alien nucleus of substance or energy, formless or otherwise, kept alive by imperceptible or immaterial subtractions from the life-force or bodily tissue and fluids of other and more palpably living things
evidence.paraphrase: The entity is theorized as a nucleus of substance/energy sustained by drawing life-force from living beings.

evidence.quote: a large and specially fitted Crookes tube operated by powerful storage batteries and provided with peculiar screens and reflectors, in case it proved intangible and opposable only by vigorously destructive ether radiations
evidence.paraphrase: They describe a Crookes-tube apparatus designed to attack the entity with ether radiations if it is intangible.

evidence.quote: Not till my adult years did my uncle set before me the notes and data which he had collected concerning the shunned house.
evidence.paraphrase: The uncle had systematically collected notes and data about the house.

evidence.quote: I turned my attention to early town records and deeds with a zeal more penetrating than that which my uncle had occasionally shown in the same work.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator researches town records and deeds to trace the site's history.

evidence.quote: It was our idea that our continued nocturnal presence would call forth whatever malign entity lurked there; and that being prepared, we could dispose of the thing with one or the other of our provided means as soon as we had recognized and observed it sufficiently.
evidence.paraphrase: They devise a plan to provoke, observe, and then destroy the entity during a vigil.

evidence.quote: Sitting down, I tried to conjecture as nearly as sanity would let me just what had happened, and how I might end the horror, if indeed it had been real.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator reasons through the events to form a hypothesis about the phenomenon and how to end it.

evidence.quote: What I saw unnerved me most surprisingly, considering its relative triviality.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator is disturbed by his uncle's altered facial expression.

evidence.quote: It was a sense of routine which kept me from going mad. I had drilled myself in preparation for the crucial moment, and blind training saved me.
evidence.paraphrase: Facing the horror, the narrator relies on drilled routine to stay sane.

evidence.quote: That object was my uncle\u2014the venerable Elihu Whipple\u2014who with blackening and decaying features leered and gibbered at me, and reached out dripping claws to rend me
evidence.paraphrase: The uncle is being transformed and consumed by the entity.

evidence.quote: the form of my uncle had commenced a nauseous liquefaction whose essence eludes all description
evidence.paraphrase: The uncle's body dissolves into liquid before the narrator.

evidence.quote: One of earth's nethermost terrors had perished for ever; and if there be a hell, it had received at last the demon soul of an unhallowed thing.
evidence.paraphrase: The entity is destroyed, ending the long-standing horror of the house.

evidence.quote: The next spring no more pale grass and strange weeds came up in the shunned house's terraced garden, and shortly afterward Carrington Harris rented the place.
evidence.paraphrase: After the destruction, the abnormal vegetation ceases and the house becomes rentable.

evidence.quote: What, then, but some exotic emanation ; some vampirish vapor such as Exeter rustics tell of as lurking over certain churchyards?
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator concludes the phenomenon is an exotic emanation, neither matter nor ether.

evidence.quote: All along the hill people tell of the yellow day, when virulent and horrible fumes arose from the factory waste dumped in the Providence River, but I know how mistaken they are as to the source.
evidence.paraphrase: The public attributes the fumes to factory waste, while the narrator knows the true supernatural cause.

evidence.quote: The surface I uncovered was fishy and glassy\u2014a kind of semi-putrid congealed jelly with suggestions of translucency.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator describes the physical substance of the buried entity uncovered by digging.

evidence.quote: And as I patted down the last spadeful of mold, I shed the first of the many tears with which I have paid unaffected tribute to my beloved uncle's memory.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator weeps in grief for his uncle after finishing the destruction.
